item.title: Researchers Introduce PFArena Benchmark for Model-Assisted Protein Modification
item.description:
Researchers Introduce PFArena Benchmark for Model-Assisted Protein Modification

Researchers have introduced PFArena, a benchmark designed to evaluate the performance of various models in protein modification tasks.

🔍 Overview

PFArena consists of four controlled task interfaces that cover two primary areas:

  • Single-mutant generation
  • Multi-mutant ranking

To reflect different research scenarios based on prior experimental context, the benchmark provides varying levels of mutation fitness data.

⚙️ Key details

The study assessed a total of 17 models across three families using complementary metrics to measure overall and peak protein modification performance:

Model Family Number of Models Observed Performance Strengths
PLMs 6 Proficiency in open-ended single-mutant generation via protein-specific priors
LLMs 6 Strong performance in multi-mutant ranking, especially with target-specific fitness data
LLM-based agents 5 Strong performance in multi-mutant ranking, especially with target-specific fitness data

Regardless of the family, all models faced fundamental challenges as mutation depth and search-space size increased.

🚀 Availability

The code and benchmark suite have been released to support reproducible research in model-assisted protein modification.

Source: PFArena: Benchmarking Language Models for Protein Modification

item.title: Anthropic's Claude AI Discovers New Enzyme System in DNA Sequences
item.description:
Anthropic’s Claude AI Discovers New Enzyme System in DNA Sequences

Anthropic has announced that its AI, Claude, has autonomously discovered a new enzyme system similar to the machinery used in the gene-editing tool Crispr.

⚙️ Key details

  • Discovery: A previously uncharacterized enzyme system found in bacteriophages (viruses that infect bacteria).
  • Resources used: Nearly 1,000 Claude agents processed 210 million tokens over a period of 21 hours.
  • Method: Claude searched through a massive database of DNA sequences until one agent identified and flagged an unusual repeating pattern for human review.
  • Human involvement: Anthropic scientists were limited to the initial prompt and the subsequent lab work.

💡 Why it matters

This discovery is the first result from Anthropic’s newly-launched wet lab and serves as an early test of Claude’s usefulness for science as the company prepares to go public. While Anthropic is still working to understand the function of the enzyme system, the company stated it was important to share the findings early to demonstrate Claude’s capabilities and provide the community with insight into their work.

#Anthropic #Claude #AI #Biotechnology #Enzymes

Source: Anthropic’s biolab made a discovery it’s comparing to Crispr
